source_batch.unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 2: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Classify a payment document as a note, bill or cheque using its operative promise or order

facts.statement: A note contains the maker's unconditional undertaking to pay a certain money sum; a bill contains an unconditional direction to another identified person to pay. A cheque is a bill on a specified banker, payable on demand, and includes qualifying electronic cheques and truncated cheque images.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 153–154; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: A note contains the maker's unconditional undertaking to pay a certain money sum; a bill contains an unconditional direction to another identified person to pay. A cheque is a bill on a specified banker, payable on demand, and includes qualifying electronic cheques and truncated cheque images.

payload.title: Start with the obligation, then identify the instrument
payload.core_explanation_md:
When checking a payment document, ask who undertakes to pay. A **promissory note** records the maker's own unconditional payment undertaking. A **bill of exchange** directs another identified person to pay. Both require writing, the relevant signature, a certain money sum and an identifiable recipient. A document that only records an unpaid balance does not establish the payment undertaking required for a note.

A **cheque** belongs to the bill family, with two extra defining features: the drawee is a specified banker and payment is on demand. Classifying every bank-related document as a cheque would miss these conditions.

self_check.prompt_text: What separates the obligation in a note from the obligation in a bill?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A note is the maker's undertaking; a bill directs another person to pay.

payload.title: Electronic form and truncation describe different routes
payload.core_explanation_md:
A cheque created electronically under the statutory signature requirements is different from an image made from an existing paper cheque. **Truncation** starts with the paper cheque: an electronic image replaces its further physical movement during clearing.

For a branch reviewer, the first task is to identify which route produced the record. A scanned document is not automatically an electronically drawn cheque. Nor does digitisation remove the need to check the underlying instrument and the duties attached to its processing.

self_check.prompt_text: Does imaging an existing paper cheque make it an electronically drawn cheque?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It produces the image of a truncated paper cheque; electronic drawing is a separate statutory category.

payload.stem_md: A supplier asks a bank to classify three documents: a signed undertaking by its customer, a signed direction to a trade buyer, and a demand-payment direction to a specified bank. Which classification follows the obligation in each?

options.text_md: Bill, note, cheque
options.explanation_md: This reverses the first two: the customer's own undertaking is a note; a direction to the trade buyer is a bill.

options.text_md: Note, cheque, bill other than cheque
options.explanation_md: The trade buyer is not identified as a banker, while the final demand direction has the defining cheque features.

options.text_md: Note, bill, cheque
options.explanation_md: The first promises payment, the second orders another person to pay, and the third is a demand bill on a specified banker.

options.text_md: Cheque, bill, note
options.explanation_md: The first does not direct a banker to pay, and the third directs payment rather than recording the maker's own promise.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The first promises payment, the second orders another person to pay, and the third is a demand bill on a specified banker.

payload.stem_md: A branch receives an image generated while a paper cheque is being cleared. The paper will remain at the presenting end. Which description best identifies this arrangement?

options.text_md: Truncation substitutes the image for further physical movement
options.explanation_md: The process begins with a paper cheque and replaces its onward physical movement with an electronic image.

options.text_md: The original cheque was necessarily drawn electronically
options.explanation_md: An image generated from paper does not show that the cheque was originally drawn in electronic form.

options.text_md: The image converts the cheque into a promissory note
options.explanation_md: Changing the clearing medium does not replace the drawer's order with a maker's payment undertaking.

options.text_md: The bank may omit all checks because no paper travels
options.explanation_md: Truncation changes transmission; it does not remove instrument verification or statutory duties.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The process begins with a paper cheque and replaces its onward physical movement with an electronic image.

payload.stem_md: A credit officer sees a signed ledger confirmation admitting an outstanding balance. It contains no payment undertaking. Why is classifying it immediately as a promissory note unsafe?

options.text_md: Only a bank may make a promissory note
options.explanation_md: The definition does not reserve the role of maker to banks; the operative undertaking is the missing feature here.

options.text_md: Every promissory note must direct a third party to pay
options.explanation_md: A direction to another person describes a bill; a note instead contains the maker's undertaking.

options.text_md: A note must include a promise to supply goods
options.explanation_md: The statutory subject is payment of money only; a goods obligation does not supply the missing payment undertaking.

options.text_md: Acknowledging a balance does not by itself supply the required undertaking
options.explanation_md: The officer must inspect the operative words; evidence of debt alone cannot replace the unconditional payment undertaking.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The officer must inspect the operative words; evidence of debt alone cannot replace the unconditional payment undertaking.
